behavior: For both Claude and Codex retained conversations, a control client and a dashboard read the same page; a different run is NotFound; a page before the start or a wrong conversation identity is Conflict; a same-run reference change after retention cannot splice pages; provider history files are never written; the session stays live and acknowledges terminal input.
failure_caught: A transcript page could mix a moved/renamed provider file with the retained conversation (showing another conversation's text) or could write to provider history, and stale pages could splice unrelated content.
criticality_reason: Splicing another conversation into a retained transcript is a privacy/integrity breach of conversation content (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/transcript.rs:88-260).
signal_reason: Asserts exact entry vectors, identity equality per page, and NotFound/Conflict for stale run, page and identity, with byte equality of the history file (tests/server_lifecycle.rs:20640-20820).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering transcript paging identity and stale-page rejection for both providers (tests/server_lifecycle.rs:20592-20837).
fidelity_reason: Real retained conversation files, real control/dashboard sockets and real agent children (tests/server_lifecycle.rs:20597-20640).
recommendation_reason: Grounded identity and staleness assertions with file-immutability evidence.

behavior: A script installed as the fixture executable checks that HOME equals OVRCR_HOME without the instance suffix, SHELL is /bin/sh, the fixture claude directory heads PATH, and nine agent-related variables are absent; the fixture CLI run succeeds.
failure_caught: The fixture could leak the developer's real HOME, shell or agent profiles into a CLI run, making results depend on the machine (and potentially reading real credentials).
criticality_reason: Test-infrastructure correctness only: a broken environment makes other tests flaky or machine-dependent (tests/support/live.rs:163-197).
signal_reason: One script with nine explicit negative checks plus a success status (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:303-325).
uniqueness_reason: Only row asserting the fixture command environment itself; per-test overrides are covered indirectly (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:303-330).
fidelity_reason: Runs the fixture command with a stand-in executable; no OVRCR product code is exercised (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:310-325).
recommendation_reason: Cheap harness invariant test; no retention gate applies.

behavior: A dashboard executable that closes all stdio, sleeps briefly and exits 23 makes OuterDashboard::start fail with an error naming the closed PTY and the exit code, instead of reporting readiness.
failure_caught: A dashboard that dies during startup could be treated as ready (tests then drive a dead UI) or the failure could omit the exit code.
criticality_reason: Startup-readiness misdetection makes dashboard acceptance tests flaky or misleading, a bounded harness failure (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:500-560).
signal_reason: Asserts the two error substrings and that start returns Err (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:333-371).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering early child-exit during dashboard readiness (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:333-371).
fidelity_reason: Real PTY child with a script standing in for the dashboard; the subject is the harness, not shipped behaviour (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:340-360).
recommendation_reason: Grounded readiness-negative assertion for the harness.

behavior: From a real dashboard, s opens Agents, filter text selects agent-a, Enter attaches to it in Terminal mode, typed input reaches only that session; the search then selects agent-b and its input reaches only agent-b, never the previous child.
failure_caught: Search input could leak into the previously selected child, or the selection could attach to the wrong session (typing into the wrong agent).
criticality_reason: Routing user keystrokes into the wrong live session can run commands in the wrong workspace (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1200-1320).
signal_reason: Asserts panel closure, Terminal mode and terminal text isolation in both sessions (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:940-985).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering the search-select-type round trip with a leak check (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:927-987).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard in an outer PTY with real sessions and terminal reads (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:929-950).
recommendation_reason: Grounded end-to-end routing assertions.

behavior: With a verified GUI input profile, Command+1/Command+9/Command-release packets typed while in a real Agent session do not invoke the Control-only jump: the following text reaches agent-a, no Session selected appears, and agent-b receives nothing.
failure_caught: Command-modified digit events could be folded onto the Control-only jump gesture, jumping the user out of the terminal and routing later input elsewhere.
criticality_reason: A wrong jump leaves the user typing into a different session than they believe (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/keymap.rs:419-500).
signal_reason: Asserts the agent receives the marker, no selection footer, and the other agent has no payload (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1000-1030).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering Command vs Control modifier separation for jump (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:990-1032).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard with the verified GUI profile and real Kitty CSI-u packets (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:995-1015).
recommendation_reason: Grounded modifier-separation assertions on real key packets.

behavior: In Terminal mode Ctrl-o belongs to the program; Ctrl-g then Ctrl-o opens Quick message; Shift+Enter splits lines, a bracketed paste becomes its own line, Escape cancels back to Browse and the session receives none of those bytes; the DB has no operator conversation.
failure_caught: Multiline composition could be sent to the terminal instead of the composer, or a cancelled Quick message could create an operator conversation and leak the draft.
criticality_reason: Sending composed text to a shell instead of the composer executes unintended commands; a cancelled draft must not persist (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/keymap.rs:419-500).
signal_reason: Asserts three separate rendered lines, Escape restoration, absence of the text in the target terminal, and a DB count of zero (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1130-1190).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering Quick-message multiline composition and Escape cleanup (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1122-1191).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY with real key encoding and a real SQLite instance (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1124-1150).
recommendation_reason: Grounded composition/cleanup assertions with durable-state check.

behavior: With the final SetView Ok withheld by a proxy, at the end of the search wait, keyboard and paste input are rejected with a visible notice and a queued cutover burst is also discarded; after release the dashboard enters Terminal mode and only post-gate input reaches agent-b; neither child ever sees the loading input.
failure_caught: Input typed while a pane is still loading could be buffered and replayed into the target, or lost with the game visible only as silent data loss.
criticality_reason: Replaying loading-time input into a newly focused agent runs commands the user typed at a different screen (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1200-1320).
signal_reason: Asserts rejection notices, absence of all four sentinel payloads in both sessions, consumed confirmation Enter, and post-gate delivery (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1200-1255).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering input discarding at the view-acknowledgement cutover (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1194-1259).
fidelity_reason: Real view proxy holding the production Ok, real dashboard PTY and two real agents (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1196-1220).
recommendation_reason: Decisive no-replay assertions across a real acknowledgement barrier.

behavior: Two agents get accepted reports: agent-a-unread has Unread, agent-z-input has WaitingInput. The Agents list shows both, ranks the input-needed session above the alphabetical Unread one, Enter lands in that session, input reaches only it, Unread survives and the input request remains after navigation.
failure_caught: Attention ordering could rank the wrong session (sending the user to the wrong agent) or navigation could clear Unread/resolve a pending request as a side effect.
criticality_reason: Misranking attention sends the user to the wrong live session, and clearing requests on navigation fabricates a decision (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/session/reporting.rs:88-205).
signal_reason: Asserts effective activity, screen ordering by index of the two rows, destination delivery and full Unread/request equality after navigation (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1270-1470).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering attention ranking with real accepted reports and real jump destination (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1262-1474).
fidelity_reason: Real supervisor reserve/hello/bind frames, real PTYs and a real dashboard PTY (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1264-1350).
recommendation_reason: Grounded ranking and no-side-effect assertions with real reporting frames.

behavior: With the fixture at exactly 50 live sessions, Agents opens, 45 Down presses land on navigation-45, Enter attaches, and a payload reaches that agent only.
failure_caught: Search/navigation could fail or select the wrong row at the 50-session capacity, making the agent picker unusable at the product limit.
criticality_reason: The fifty-session guarantee is an explicit invariant; the picker must remain usable at capacity (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/mod.rs:1135-1155).
signal_reason: Asserts the exact session count, the highlighted row after 45 moves and destination delivery; a wrong intermediate row would be missed only if it converges (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1485-1510).
uniqueness_reason: Only row exercising the agent picker at the fifty-session limit (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1477-1514).
fidelity_reason: Real 50 live PTY sessions, real dashboard PTY and real key input (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1479-1495).
recommendation_reason: The only capacity-level picker protection; retain.

behavior: A branch-only shortcut on a repo whose remote default is `trunk` creates feature/wizard from origin/trunk (not main), leaves it selected in Browse, creates exactly one Terminal-kind local session named local, opens it, and the shell runs in that worktree on that branch.
failure_caught: The workspace could be created from the wrong base (main instead of the remote default), or the shortcut could auto-create agent sessions or the wrong number of terminals.
criticality_reason: Branching from the wrong base silently builds work on the wrong history, a major workflow defect (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/mod.rs:2325-2410).
signal_reason: Asserts the created session set, branch name, HEAD equality with origin/trunk and a shell marker in the terminal (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1520-1660).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering the branch-only workspace shortcut's base resolution and first terminal (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1517-1663).
fidelity_reason: Real Git repository with remote refs, real server and real PTY shell (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1519-1560).
recommendation_reason: Grounded base-ref and creation-shape assertions.

behavior: Creating an agent session with a multiline initial prompt through the New agent form reaches a fake claude: the prompt arrives as exactly one AGENT_ARG entry after an explicit `--` separator, is not used as the session name, and the branch child workspace exists.
failure_caught: A multiline prompt could be split into multiple argv items or shell-split, changing the instructions the agent receives (or letting prompt text inject arguments).
criticality_reason: Prompt/argv confusion alters the agent's instructions and can inject flags, a major correctness/authority issue (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/agent_models.rs:520-560).
signal_reason: Asserts exactly one occurrence of the full prompt argument, its position after the separator, and the session identity (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1660-1760).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering initial-prompt argv fidelity through the branch child and compiled CLI (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1669-1769).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard form input, real compiled CLI/server and a scripted claude that prints its argv (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1671-1700).
recommendation_reason: Decisive single-argument assertion for a security-relevant boundary.

behavior: A two-pane split is driven through the real dashboard: both panes receive their own input and show their own acknowledgements, pane headers and separators follow focus, resizes to 100x30 and 80x30 then 120x40 change the children's reported sizes exactly, closing one pane removes the separator, and a reattach restores one pane then rebuilds the split with both children otherwise untouched (same pids).
failure_caught: Split input could be routed to the wrong pane, resize could resize the wrong PTY (or not resize), and closing/reattaching could restart sessions or leave stale separators.
criticality_reason: Misdirected split input or wrong PTY geometry makes multi-pane work unusable and can corrupt an agent TUI (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1-120).
signal_reason: Child-reported stty sizes, per-rect content assertions, separator checks and pid stability across detach/reattach (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1835-2000).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering split geometry and input routing through the outer PTY with real children (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1831-2006).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY, two real shells reporting kernel PTY sizes, real detach/reattach (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:1833-1860).
recommendation_reason: Grounded multi-pane geometry and identity assertions.

behavior: A live session's history: PageUp freezes history and older rows become visible; live output arriving while frozen marks 'new output' without moving the frozen rows; a resize keeps the frozen rows and reflows the status; leaving history shows the live output again.
failure_caught: Frozen history could shift or lose rows when new output arrives or the window resizes, so the user reads a corrupted transcript.
criticality_reason: A frozen history page that moves under the user corrupts the transcript they are reading (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/session/mod.rs:1065-1095).
signal_reason: Asserts old rows plus the new-output marker after live output, their persistence across resize, a changed status line, and live output after exit (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2015-2185).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering history freeze under live output and resize through the dashboard (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2009-2189).
fidelity_reason: Real PTY producing 100 rows, real dashboard PTY and FIFO-driven live output (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2011-2040).
recommendation_reason: Grounded frozen-history stability assertions.

behavior: A 40x125 historic page is copied through the dashboard: the cursor walks rows 1-16 and columns 1-126, selection extends to row 17 columns 128-130, y emits exactly the expected OSC52 payload spanning page and tile boundaries, the notice appears, and moving the cursor after copy does not re-emit.
failure_caught: Cross-page/tile selection could produce truncated, duplicated or misaligned clipboard text, and copying could re-emit on cursor movement.
criticality_reason: Truncated or duplicated clipboard text silently corrupts what the user pastes into another program (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/copy.rs:198-470).
signal_reason: Byte-exact OSC52 expectation computed with the production writer across row/col boundaries plus a post-copy no-reemit check (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2300-2380).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering copy across page and tile boundaries with byte-exact output (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2192-2384).
fidelity_reason: Real history rows over the server protocol and a real dashboard PTY emitting OSC52 (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2194-2230).
recommendation_reason: Byte-exact cross-boundary assertion; retain.

behavior: A broad outer-PTY sweep: paste, typed input, 20 command echoes and 20 single raw keys are observed and p95 latency stays under 100ms; raw mode works; mouse session receives mouse tokens; a resize to 120x40 re-enters Terminal mode and reports 36x80; detach and reattach restore the row.
failure_caught: PTY input/echo could stall (p95 over 100ms), raw-mode keys could be lost, resize could leave the pane unusable, or reattach could lose the session.
criticality_reason: A slow or stuck input path makes the terminal unusable in practice; latency is the only observed signal for it (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/event_loop.rs:1-120).
signal_reason: Broad smoke with two latency percentiles, paste/input/mouse/resize/reattach checks; it would pass many wrong behaviours outside those paths (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2545-2595).
uniqueness_reason: Aggregate wrapper re-covering paste/input/mouse/resize; its only distinct assertion is the visible-echo latency distribution (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2540-2598).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard in an outer PTY with real sessions and mouse packets (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2542-2560).
recommendation_reason: Kept for the latency boundary; most of its other assertions are subsumed by narrower rows, so a future consolidation into those rows is possible but not proven equivalent.

behavior: An empty dashboard shows the welcome and register-repository hint without a socket line; the Events overlay lists Home and Socket paths under the fixture root as `~/...`; closing it removes them; opening the repository form and cancelling restores BROWSE.
failure_caught: The empty-state could print absolute or wrong instance paths (already-fixed leak) or leave an overlay stuck.
criticality_reason: Wrong empty-state paths are a bounded UI/leak issue with the Events overlay as evidence (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1-80).
signal_reason: Asserts welcome text, absence of Socket in welcome, exact `~/` path strings in Events and overlay dismissal (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2545-2595).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering empty-instance path presentation (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2540-2598).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard against an empty isolated instance (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2546-2560).
recommendation_reason: Grounded empty-state path assertions.

behavior: Copy mode from Browse: help/close and form cancel preserve the live session snapshot; [gv then six l then y emits exactly the OSC52 payload for WAITING, Escape returns to Browse; input then reaches the session; after reattach the retained screen is copyable at the same pane coordinates, and F12 clears the startup note without entering Terminal mode.
failure_caught: Copy selections could capture the wrong cells or the reattached view could mis-map coordinates, producing wrong clipboard text; cancelling forms could disturb the session.
criticality_reason: Wrong copy output silently pastes incorrect text into other applications (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/copy.rs:69-200).
signal_reason: Exact OSC52 bases for two selections, screen-coordinate reconstruction after reattach, and session-text equality after cancels (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2605-2790).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering copy-mode coordinate mapping across detach/reattach (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2601-2795).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY, real session screen and real OSC52 output (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2603-2640).
recommendation_reason: Grounded coordinate/selection assertions with durable screen checks.

behavior: Pausing from the dashboard shows Paused and List reports the session Paused; after detach/reattach the pane still shows Paused; r resumes, Paused disappears, Enter enters Terminal mode and a token is acknowledged.
failure_caught: Pause state could be lost across reattach, or resume could leave input rejected while claiming Running.
criticality_reason: A paused session that silently resumes or stays paused makes input availability unpredictable (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/mod.rs:871-880).
signal_reason: Asserts screen and List phase, reattach persistence, and a real input acknowledgement after resume (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2800-2860).
uniqueness_reason: Dashboard round-trip variant; the server-level pause rows cover group signals and removal gates (tests/server_lifecycle.rs:2725-2896).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY, real session and real detach/reattach (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2802-2820).
recommendation_reason: Grounded pause/resume round trip with input proof.

behavior: External CLI pause makes the live dashboard show Paused; external resume clears it in BROWSE; external kill makes the dashboard show Exited; detach works throughout.
failure_caught: Dashboard redraw could miss externally driven phase changes (stale Running/Paused) or fail to show exit.
criticality_reason: A dashboard that does not reflect external lifecycle changes misleads the user about whether a session is running (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/mod.rs:871-880).
signal_reason: Three CLI actions each asserted by a screen transition within 3s; no phase equality is checked beyond the label (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2880-2915).
uniqueness_reason: Only row driving phase changes purely from the CLI while the dashboard is live (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2865-2919).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled CLI against a real server with a real dashboard PTY (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2867-2890).
recommendation_reason: Grounded external-change redraw coverage.

behavior: With the child requesting mouse reports (E), the dashboard forwards press+release with exact SGR bytes to the child and disables capture on D; a mouse report after disable is not forwarded; on a plain shell the wheel opens the dashboard's own frozen history instead.
failure_caught: Mouse bytes could be forwarded to a child that did not request them (corrupting its input) or withheld when it did.
criticality_reason: Forwarding mouse reports to a program that did not ask for them injects escape sequences into its input (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/input.rs:58-143).
signal_reason: Asserts exact forwarded byte strings, absence after disable, and history fallback on a plain shell (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2940-2985).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering mouse capture negotiation and exact forwarding (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2928-2987).
fidelity_reason: Real mouse fixture child, real dashboard PTY and real SGR mouse input (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2930-2950).
recommendation_reason: Decisive byte-level forwarding assertions.

behavior: After a press without release, retargeting the outbox to another session delivers exactly the captured release to the original mouse child before fresh input; the new session receives its own input; the original child never receives the new input.
failure_caught: A held mouse button retargeted to another session could leak the release (or the new input) to the original child, or leave the new child without a coherent release.
criticality_reason: Cross-session mouse state leakage injects input into the wrong child and can leave a held button stuck (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/input.rs:58-143).
signal_reason: Asserts the exact release bytes on the original child and an empty second report after the new input (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:3000-3045).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering outbox retargeting with a held mouse button (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2990-3053).
fidelity_reason: Real mouse fixture child and real dashboard PTY with two sessions (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:2992-3020).
recommendation_reason: Grounded byte-exact retarget assertions.

behavior: In a session that switched to the alternate screen, a wheel tick over the pane opens nothing (no History, no error, no message); PageUp shows a muted explanation that history is unavailable while fullscreen, with no ERROR/Conflict/internal text.
failure_caught: A wheel tick over a full-screen program could open a bogus history view or print an internal error, and PageUp could fail silently or loudly.
criticality_reason: Full-screen history gating is a bounded UX defect with a clear workaround (leave the program) (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1200-1320).
signal_reason: Asserts a 2s absence window for wheel, then the explanation text and absence of four internal strings (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:3070-3125).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering alternate-screen history gating (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:3056-3131).
fidelity_reason: Real shell entering the alternate screen through a real PTY and dashboard (tests/terminal_acceptance.rs:3058-3075).
recommendation_reason: Grounded negative and explanation assertions.

behavior: An assigned child is view-only: a passive split/focus/resize/hide never changes its run, phase or default control, and a bracketed paste sent before takeover never reaches it. H (takeover) shows Human control, Enter enters Terminal mode, a marker reaches the child, then A (return) enters a pending reconciliation barrier and further input is rejected; afterwards the child's run and Running phase are unchanged with owner Controller, epoch 3 and a HumanReturn barrier.
failure_caught: Viewing could mutate control ownership or let input through before takeover; return could leave control unclaimed or let input race reconciliation.
criticality_reason: View-only enforcement is an ownership boundary: input before takeover or a stuck return can send commands to an agent the user does not control (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/delegation_control.rs:1-140).
signal_reason: Asserts control equality before takeover, absence of the forbidden payload, and post-return owner/epoch/barrier plus run/phase stability (tests/terminal_acceptance/assignment_control.rs:150-400).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering the assignment-control takeover/return state machine end to end (tests/terminal_acceptance/assignment_control.rs:135-402).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard, real assigned Pi child through delegation and real server control frames (tests/terminal_acceptance/assignment_control.rs:30-90).
recommendation_reason: Grounded ownership invariants with real input attempts.

behavior: The dashboard requests keyboard reporting; a shifted `;` encoded with the negotiated alternate-key flag (or the base key without it) opens the Command palette.
failure_caught: A conforming terminal's shifted key could fail to open the palette because the dashboard either ignored alternate keys or required them.
criticality_reason: A browse shortcut failing is a bounded UX defect with other ways to open the palette (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/keymap.rs:137-180).
signal_reason: Reads the dashboard's requested flags and sends the matching encoding, then asserts the palette title (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:44-46).
uniqueness_reason: One of several shifted/legacy encodings of the same shortcut; distinct negotiation branch (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:44-59).
fidelity_reason: Real compiled dashboard in an outer PTY receiving real CSI-u bytes (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:6-20).
recommendation_reason: Grounded negotiation branch; cheap.

behavior: With the same negotiation, a shifted `/` opens the Which-key overlay help.
failure_caught: The question-mark shortcut could be unreachable with alternate-key reporting.

signal_reason: Asserts the help overlay title after the negotiated encoding (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:49-51).

failure_caught: Alternate-key control events could be misread as their base character (typing a literal `C`) or fail to trigger the control shortcut (Ctrl-D deleting text).
criticality_reason: Misdecoded control keys in the composer can delete a draft or submit unintended text (bounded, recoverable) (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/input.rs:6-57).

failure_caught: iTerm2 control-hold digits could fail to select (or select the wrong agent) on the tested version, or release input could reach the wrong session.
criticality_reason: A terminal-specific jump regression is a bounded UX defect with the Agents picker as a workaround (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/keymap.rs:137-180).
signal_reason: Asserts the labeled sidebar, Session selected, Terminal mode and destination-only delivery (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:107-160).

behavior: With iTerm metadata behind TMUX, a Control packet plus digit plus release must not invoke browse actions: the Command palette opens from a later shifted packet, and no Session selected or jump labels appear.
failure_caught: Multiplexer-mangled iTerm metadata could be interpreted as a control-hold jump, moving the user out of the terminal and misrouting later input.
criticality_reason: A false jump triggered by terminal metadata moves focus and routes subsequent input to another session (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/keymap.rs:137-180).
signal_reason: Asserts the palette result, absence of Session selected and absence of jump labels (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:180-196).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering tmux-wrapped iTerm metadata rejection (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:174-198).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY with TMUX/TERM_PROGRAM environment and real CSI-u packets (tests/terminal_acceptance/keyboard_protocol.rs:180-196).
recommendation_reason: Decisive metadata-rejection assertions.

behavior: An Operator conversation holds an unsent draft; Control+1 select and repeat/another digit do not type into the draft or the target; the agent receives only post-release input; returning to Operator restores the exact draft.
failure_caught: Jump digits or repeats could become composer text or reach the target agent before release, and the Operator draft could be lost.
criticality_reason: Losing an Operator draft loses user composition, and pre-release digits reaching an agent execute unintended text (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1200-1320).
signal_reason: Asserts no target lines containing the digits, exact draft preservation, and no OPERATOR text in the old program or target (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_operator.rs:60-125).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering jump from an Operator draft with repeat-digit fencing (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_operator.rs:17-130).
fidelity_reason: Real dashboard PTY, real Operator conversation and real agent (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_operator.rs:19-45).
recommendation_reason: Grounded draft-preservation and digit-fencing assertions.

behavior: Jumping to a retained exited agent inspects it without restarting: run and Exited/pid-none stay identical over 300ms, the process-group set is unchanged, and held keys never reach it; jumping to a running agent delivers only post-release input to that agent.
failure_caught: Selecting a retained row could restart the agent (new run/process) or leak held input into it, and the running-jump could deliver to the wrong session.
criticality_reason: A retained-row jump that restarts work would spawn a process the user only meant to inspect (crates/ovrcr-runtime/src/server/mod.rs:1466-1515).
signal_reason: Asserts run/phase/pid stability, sorted group-set equality, selection-leak absence, and destination-only delivery (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_retained.rs:150-230).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering retained vs running jump destinations with process-group evidence (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_retained.rs:95-235).
fidelity_reason: Real exited and running PTY sessions, real dashboard PTY and group enumeration (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_retained.rs:97-140).
recommendation_reason: Grounded no-restart/no-leak assertions with real process state.

behavior: With ten agents, Control-hold labels [1]..[9] on the first nine only and leaves the tenth visible but unlabelled; digit 0 reports no visible agent for that number without selecting; digit 9 selects and, once the gated view acknowledges after Control-up, only that agent receives the post-release payload while every other agent receives nothing.
failure_caught: Out-of-range digits could select the wrong agent, and pre-acknowledgement input could reach the destination or an unintended one.
criticality_reason: A single-digit jump mis-selecting or leaking pre-release input sends commands to the wrong live agent (crates/ovrcr-tui/src/dashboard/state.rs:1200-1320).
signal_reason: Asserts per-row labels, the zero hint without selection, gated acknowledgement, and a scan of all ten terminals for leakage (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_single_digit.rs:25-105).
uniqueness_reason: Only row covering the nine-digit label bound and zero case (tests/terminal_acceptance/session_jump_single_digit.rs:4-111).
